policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: - Determine the cube's motion from the last two frames shown at this step, in this order. (1) If the cube is on different sides of the target in those two frames, it is passing the target right now and its next motion is outward: classify it as MOVING AWAY, whatever the distances are.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: - Determine the cube's motion from a pair of positions, in this order. Form the pair first: when two or more frames are shown at this step, the pair is the last two frames shown; when exactly one frame is shown, the earlier member of the pair is the carried-in memory (position last_cube_x, side cube_side, time last_t) and the later member is the shown frame, so the x change is cube_x minus last_cube_x and the timestep gap is t of this frame minus last_t. (1) If the cube is on different sides of the target in the two members of the pair (for a single-frame step: the carried-in cube_side differs from the side in this frame), it is passing the target right now and its next motion is outward: classify it as MOVING AWAY, whatever the distances are.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: (2) Otherwise compute |cube_x - target_x| at each of the two frames, take the change (later minus earlier) and divide by the number of timesteps between the two frames: this is the outward rate in px per timestep (negative if the distance shrank).
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: (2) Otherwise compute |cube_x - target_x| at each member of the pair, take the change (later minus earlier) and divide by the timestep gap between them: this is the outward rate in px per timestep (negative if the distance shrank).

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: (returning, stopped, or a fast cube drifting outward at no more than about 1 px per timestep). No point is needed.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: (returning, stopped, or a fast cube drifting outward at no more than about 1 px per timestep). No point is needed. A step that shows a single frame is common right after the step at which the cube was seen nearing its extreme; when crossings == N-1 and the pair formed from memory gives a tiny or negative outward rate, that single-frame step is the press moment, not a reason to wait. Showing only one frame is never by itself a reason to choose B.

policy_prompt_for_memory.description: Write the cube's x-coordinate in the last frame shown at this step (the scene at this decision step), as a plain number. Overwrite it every step; at the first step read it from the single frame shown. It is read at the next step only when that step shows a single frame and so has no pair of frames of its own to compare. e.g. 206
Write the timestep index t of the scene at this decision step (the last frame shown). Overwrite it every step; at the first step write 0. e.g. 54

edits.modify_from: Take the carried-in peak_speed (0 if memory is empty). For each pair of consecutive frames shown at this step, compute |cube_x(later) - cube_x(earlier)| divided by the number of timesteps between the two frames. Do not pair any frame shown here with a frame from an earlier step. Write the largest of the carried-in value and all these per-pair speeds, rounded to one decimal. It never decreases. At the first step (one frame only) write 0. e.g. 3.8
edits.modify_to: Take the carried-in peak_speed (0 if memory is empty). List every consecutive pair of frames shown at this step, starting with the pair formed by the first and second frames shown (the first frame shown is an execution step, not the previous scene, so it is paired normally) and ending with the pair formed by the last two frames shown. Do not pair any frame shown here with a frame from an earlier step. For each pair write the x change |cube_x(later) - cube_x(earlier)|, the timestep gap between the two frames, and the quotient rounded to one decimal with halves rounding up (3.875 -> 3.9). Write the largest of the carried-in value and all these quotients. It never decreases. When only one frame is shown (including the first step, where the carried-in value is 0), write the carried-in value unchanged. e.g. 3.9

edits.modify_from: write the largest such value seen so far, rounded to one decimal.

Keeping last_cube_x and last_t instead lets the single-frame step use the same rate-and-peak_speed classification committed in rounds 1 and 2, so nothing earlier is undone: the side-flip test, the 1 px per timestep rate threshold, the 2.5 px per timestep peak_speed threshold and the within-step pairing for peak_speed all stand.
